[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cheese pairing is subjective and depends on individual tastes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Classic cheese pairings include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Cheddar with crackers, apples, grapes, or beer  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Brie with bread, honey, or berries  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Parmesan with pasta, risotto, or salad  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Blue cheese with pears, walnuts, or honey  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some cheeses are versatile and can be paired with almost anything.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested lesser-known cheese pairings include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Ricotta with roasted beets, drizzled with honey  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Feta with watermelon, topped with a balsamic glaze  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Gouda with sliced pears, sprinkled with cinnamon  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Goat cheese with grilled peaches, topped with a basil-infused syrup  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Halloumi with grilled figs, drizzled with maple syrup  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Camembert with candied pecans and apple slices  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Manchego with quince paste and sliced almonds  
[USER] User expressed excitement about the cheese pairing suggestions and plans to try them with friends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for creating a great cheese board include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Include a variety of cheeses of different styles, textures, and flavors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Add complementary accompaniments such as crackers, bread, nuts, fruits, honey, and charcuterie.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Arrange the cheese and accompaniments aesthetically on a wooden board or slate.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Take cheeses out of the fridge at least an hour before serving for optimal flavor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Provide an ample quantity of cheese, around 3-5 types in various sizes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Choose compatible wines for pairing with the cheese, matching the intensity of the wine with the cheese flavor.
